title: 11 Legal AI Tools for Specific Legal Workflows in 2026
summary: Compare 11 legal AI tools by workflow, including research, patent litigation, contracts, eDiscovery, analytics, practice management, and plaintiff work.
body_markdown:
Legal AI now spans several distinct product categories. A research assistant, contract lifecycle platform, and patent litigation workspace may all use AI, yet they rely on different sources and produce different work. A useful shortlist starts with the job, required evidence, final deliverable, security needs, and buying model. Those distinctions matter more than a long feature count or a generic “best overall” label.


## Key takeaways


- Match the product to the work product you need.
- Patent litigation teams should shortlist our AI workspace when their work runs from prior art or product evidence to source-linked invalidity and infringement analysis, claim charts, and litigation drafting.
- Legal research tools need authoritative legal sources. Matter analysis tools need traceable links to the uploaded record.
- Most broad legal AI platforms use quote-based pricing. A few products publish self-serve or usage-based rates.
- Attorney review remains part of the workflow. Faster generation has little value when the output requires reconstruction.


## What legal AI tools actually do


“Legal AI” describes a set of tools rather than one product category. The most useful distinction is the job each system completes and the evidence it can reach.


Workflow Required source material Useful output


Legal research Case law, statutes, regulations, citators, secondary sources Cited research answer, memo, or draft


Patent litigation Patents, prosecution history, non-patent literature, product evidence Prior art results, invalidity or infringement analysis, claim chart


Contract drafting Current document, precedent, clause library, negotiation playbook Draft, redline, issue list, clause suggestion


Contract lifecycle management Contract repository, approval rules, business systems Routed approval, obligation record, renewal action, portfolio insight


eDiscovery Collected electronically stored information and review protocol Search results, coded review set, chronology, evidence-grounded narrative


Litigation analytics Dockets, rulings, parties, counsel, judges, outcomes Timing, motion, outcome, and behavior analysis


Practice management Matters, calendars, communications, time, billing Tasks, deadline entries, client updates, draft invoices


Practice-specific plaintiff work Case files, medical records, bills, settlement history Medical chronology, demand, case assessment, negotiation support


We have not tested these tools against a common hands-on benchmark. This desk-researched shortlist includes eleven established products that each represent a distinct legal workflow or major research environment and excludes consumer chatbots, private-beta and preview products, standalone databases without a named AI workflow, patent prosecution software, and firmwide knowledge management platforms. Features and public buying terms were checked on September 24, 2026. Availability can depend on the plan, region, rollout, and administrator settings; confirm the specific workflow before buying. Prices are in U.S. dollars unless noted otherwise.

### &AI for patent litigation


*Screenshot source:[&AI homepage](https://www.tryandai.com/) , captured September 11, 2026. Product details:[patent litigation workflows](https://www.tryandai.com/product) and[current pricing](https://www.tryandai.com/pricing) .*


Shortlist our[patent litigation AI workspace](https://www.tryandai.com/patent-litigation-ai) when the work begins with claim limitations and ends in reviewable litigation work product. Our multi-strategy prior art search covers patents and non-patent literature (NPL). We also discover publicly available product materials on the live web and chart product documents you supply. Search results feed into invalidity and infringement analysis, source-linked claim charts, and contention drafts subject to attorney review.


Attorneys can inspect pinpoint evidence, approve chart citations, edit the analysis, and export configurable claim charts to Word. Excel exports are available for adjacent artifacts, including heatmaps, saved tables, and claim constructions. Public pricing includes pay as you go at $0.40 per credit, Pro at $625 per monthly user with 2,500 credits, and custom Enterprise terms. Every plan includes the core platform. The seven-day free trial is available through self-serve pay as you go and Pro, while Enterprise terms are custom. Broad case law research, contract lifecycle management, patent prosecution, and firm billing sit outside our core.


### CoCounsel Legal for Westlaw-backed research and drafting


*Screenshot source: the official[CoCounsel Legal product page](https://legal.thomsonreuters.com/en/products/cocounsel-legal) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail:[CoCounsel Legal plans](https://legal.thomsonreuters.com/en/c/compare-cocounsel-plans-for-your-legal-team) and the[global research guide](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en-us/help/cocounsel/legal/navigation/about/use-global-research) .*


CoCounsel Legal combines Westlaw and Practical Law with a general legal workspace. Deep Research creates cited analyses from a legal question. Litigation Document Analyzer and Tabular Analysis work across uploaded material, while Westlaw Brief Builder and the Microsoft Word experience move research into drafting.


The clearest fit is a team that already treats Westlaw and Practical Law as core sources and wants AI inside that environment. The platform also organizes documents and prior work by matter. Published starting prices appear for select in-house plans, while the final package depends on content access and plan selection. For specialized jobs such as patent evidence mapping, test whether its document analysis and exports meet your requirements.


### Lexis+ with Protégé for LexisNexis research and drafting


*Screenshot source: the official[Lexis+ with Protégé product page](https://www.lexisnexis.com/en-us/products/lexis-plus-protege.page) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the Lexis+ with Protégé product page and[workflow guide](https://www.lexisnexis.com/supportandtraining/cfs-file/__key/telligent-evolution-components-attachments/01-88-00-00-00-00-14-96/CA-Lexis_2B00_-with-Protege-_2D00_-Workflow_2D00_Powered-Legal-AI-for-Every-Role-v3.pdf) .*


Lexis+ with Protégé, renamed from Lexis+ AI in February 2026, brings research, drafting, and document analysis into one LexisNexis workspace. It draws on primary law, secondary sources, Practical Guidance, Shepard’s citation treatment, web material, and connected organizational documents. Protégé can produce full transactional and litigation drafts and work inside Microsoft 365.


This option fits firms that depend on LexisNexis content and want research, citator signals, and drafting connected. Vault supports large document sets, and document management system connections can add firm knowledge. Pricing is customized and a trial is available. Protégé is an AI layer across several LexisNexis products, so buyers still need to identify which underlying subscriptions support the intended workflow.


### Harvey for firmwide enterprise legal work


*Screenshot source: the official[Harvey homepage](https://www.harvey.ai/) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the[Harvey workspace guide](https://help.harvey.ai/articles/getting-started-with-harvey) .*


Harvey is a horizontal legal AI platform for large firms and corporate legal departments. Assistant handles questions, analysis, and drafting. Vault organizes and analyzes large document collections. Review Tables extract structured answers across documents, and Workflow Agents standardize recurring multistep tasks. Harvey for Microsoft extends work into Word and Outlook.


Its breadth makes sense when one enterprise platform must support several practice groups and connect to firm knowledge. Available knowledge sources include licensed legal content, public sources, organizational material, and selected web sources. Harvey sells through an enterprise process with custom pricing rather than a public self-serve plan. Deployment value therefore depends heavily on integrations, governed knowledge, workflow design, and adoption across enough users.


### Paxton for self-serve U.S. research and drafting


*Screenshot source: the official[Paxton homepage](https://www.paxton.ai/) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the[Research Coverage page](https://www.paxton.ai/coverage) and[Paxton plan and product FAQ](https://help.paxton.ai/help/other-topics/frequently-asked-questions) .*


Paxton combines U.S. legal research, drafting, document analysis, and medical chronology or billing-summary work in a web assistant. Its research coverage includes federal and state law, regulations, appellate and other court material, and selected administrative decisions. Research responses link to authority, while uploaded files can feed summaries and drafts.


The self-serve buying path separates Paxton from many enterprise-only platforms. An individual plan is $499 per user monthly or $2,999 annually, with a seven-day trial. Enterprise terms are available through sales. Paxton is most relevant when one attorney or a smaller firm wants several common workflows in one subscription. Teams needing deep international coverage, eDiscovery-scale review, or a practice-specific production system should treat those as separate requirements.


### Spellbook for contract work in Word and Google Docs


*Screenshot source: the official[Spellbook homepage](https://spellbook.com/) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail:[Spellbook setup across Associate, Word, and Google Docs](https://help.spellbook.legal/en/articles/16446363-install-spellbook-associate-word-google-docs) .*


Spellbook supports single-document contract work in Microsoft Word and Google Docs, plus multi-document work in Associate. The Word add-in reviews language, drafts clauses, answers questions, compares terms with benchmarks, and applies saved playbooks. The Google Docs add-in supports review, playbooks, questions, and suggested redlines through its Chrome extension. Associate compares documents, revises a template against references, and answers questions across several files.


The fit is narrow and clear: recurring drafting, review, and negotiation of commercial agreements. A[seven-day trial](https://spellbook.com/pricing) is available, with custom pricing based on team size. Associate access depends on subscription entitlements. The[Google Docs guide](https://help.spellbook.legal/en/articles/15934776-install-spellbook-in-google-docs) still labels some limitations as beta and lists Draft, Compare to Market, Definitions, and Benchmarking as unavailable. Associate also offers a[Repository](https://help.spellbook.legal/en/articles/16042055-repository) for contract reports and metadata extraction. Evaluate full contract lifecycle management, eDiscovery, and matter management as separate requirements.


### Ironclad for contract lifecycle management


*Screenshot source: the official[Ironclad AI product page](https://ironcladapp.com/product/ironclad-ai) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the[Ironclad AI overview](https://support.ironcladapp.com/hc/en-us/articles/12947738534935-Ironclad-AI-Overview) and[AI credit guide](https://support.ironcladapp.com/hc/en-us/articles/42674655829655-AI-Credits-in-Ironclad) .*


Ironclad manages the contracting process from intake and drafting through approval, signature, storage, obligations, and renewal. Its no-code Workflow Designer routes work across legal and business teams. Ironclad AI includes repository questions, specialized agents, and Jurist for drafting, redlining, playbook review, risk flags, and summaries.


The CLM platform fits in-house contract operations. Pricing is customized.[Jurist requires a Jurist seat](https://legal.ironcladapp.com/fy2026-product-descriptions) and is also sold separately from CLM. Eligible AI agent actions moved to a shared credit model in September 2026, while some AI functions remain included under platform terms. The economic case depends on contract volume, workflow adoption outside legal, repository quality, integrations, and the amount of administration required.


### Everlaw for eDiscovery and investigations


*Screenshot source: the official[Everlaw AI product page](https://www.everlaw.com/product/everlaw-ai/) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the[Everlaw pricing page](https://www.everlaw.com/pricing/) ,[Deep Dive setup](https://support.everlaw.com/hc/en-us/articles/43466730645275-Enroll-and-Get-Started-with-Deep-Dive) , the[Coding Suggestions guide](https://support.everlaw.com/hc/en-us/articles/17436012380315-Everlaw-AI-Coding-Suggestions) , and the[billing and pricing FAQ](https://support.everlaw.com/hc/en-us/articles/205660765-Billing-and-Pricing-FAQ) .*


Everlaw applies AI to discovery data and the record built from it. Deep Dive answers natural-language questions across large matters with citations to underlying documents. Coding Suggestions recommends review codes with rationales. Review Assistant summarizes and extracts, while Storybuilder and Writing Assistant help teams build chronologies, arguments, and drafts grounded in selected evidence.


The platform fits litigation and investigation teams that need collection, review, production, and case preparation in one environment. Pricing is based on managed data and AI usage. Core plans include unlimited users and some single-document AI actions, while batch actions add usage charges. Deep Dive requires an Everlaw AI contract and charges credits to enroll data; it is not currently available in GovCloud. Everlaw is an evidence platform. A legal research subscription or specialist practice tool may still sit beside it.


### Lex Machina for litigation analytics


*Screenshot source: the official[Lex Machina product page](https://www.lexisnexis.com/en-us/products/lex-machina.page) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the[Lex Machina coverage and feature overview](https://www.lexisnexis.com/en-us/products/lex-machina.page) .*


Lex Machina turns court records into structured analytics about judges, courts, parties, counsel, experts, motion practice, timing, damages, and outcomes. Protégé adds natural-language access to those data. Coverage spans federal courts, selected state courts, appeals, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, and practice-specific datasets.


This product supports litigation strategy, budgeting, pitches, and outside-counsel selection. It does not perform the same job as a research assistant or matter evidence workspace. Historical patterns can sharpen a decision. They cannot establish what a court will do in a new matter. Pricing is customized through a demo.


### Clio Manage and Clio Work for firm operations and legal work


*Screenshot source: the official[Clio Legal AI page](https://www.clio.com/features/legal-ai-software/) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the[Clio pricing page](https://www.clio.com/pricing/) , the[Manage AI feature overview](https://www.clio.com/features/legal-ai-software/) ,[Clio Work guide](https://help.clio.com/hc/en-150/articles/41653068567579-Get-Started-With-Clio-Work) , and[Work subscription guide](https://help.clio.com/hc/en-us/articles/48541569005979-Manage-Subscription-and-Users-in-Clio-Work) .*


Clio now separates two complementary jobs. Clio Manage runs matters, calendars, documents, communications, time, billing, and payments. Its AI can turn court documents into calendar entries, draft client updates, organize matter activity, prioritize tasks, and prepare invoices. Clio Work handles cited legal research, document and recording analysis, timelines, and first-pass drafts from matter context.


This combination is relevant to solo, small, and midsize firms that want operations and substantive work connected. Clio advertises Manage from $49 per user per month, with AI on Core and higher plans; confirm billing terms in the quote. Clio Work offers a trial and per-user pricing through a quote, and it can run with or without Clio Manage. Firms should treat the operational and legal-work components as distinct budget decisions.


### EvenUp for personal injury case work


*Screenshot source: the official[EvenUp products page](https://www.evenuplaw.com/products/) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the EvenUp products page,[Trial page with all-in-one case-based pricing](https://www.evenuplaw.com/trial/) , and[subscription terms](https://www.evenuplaw.com/wp-content/uploads/Subscription_Terms_and_Conditions.pdf) .*


EvenUp is a practice-specific system for personal injury firms. Its product suite covers medical chronologies and bills, demands, case analysis, drafting, discovery support, settlement preparation, communication agents, workflow automation, and case management services. The system draws on case files and personal injury data rather than presenting a general legal chat interface.


The fit depends on the firm’s case type and volume. EvenUp uses all-in-one, case-based pricing supplied through sales and connects with common personal injury case management systems. Its specialization is the advantage for a qualifying practice and the limit for everyone else.


## A 2026 watchlist item: Gemini Enterprise for Legal


*Screenshot source: the official[Gemini Enterprise for Legal landing page](https://cloud.google.com/ai/legal) , captured September 11, 2026. Primary-source detail: the[launch announcement](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/introducing-gemini-enterprise-for-legal) ,[Gemini Enterprise release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes) , and[legal research guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/use-cases/legal-research) .*


Google Cloud introduced Gemini Enterprise for Legal in preview on August 25, 2026. It is a legal plugin inside Gemini Enterprise, with reusable skills, specialized agents, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors to legal research, document management, eDiscovery, contract, and other systems. Initial workflows include contract review, regulatory monitoring, playbook creation, data subject access requests, and redaction.


The platform is relevant to firms and legal departments already using Gemini Enterprise and looking for one governance layer across connected systems. It remains a preview product with contact-sales pricing, so it belongs on a watchlist rather than in a production comparison with generally available tools.


## How to choose legal AI software


### Start with the accepted work product


Name the output that must survive attorney review: a cited research memo, approved redline, produced review set, limitation-by-limitation chart, filed deadline, or client-ready demand. A product that generates fluent text can still fail if the team must rebuild the substance or format elsewhere.


### Inspect grounding at the source level


Legal citations, document references, and claim mappings need direct paths to the underlying source. In a 2025 peer-reviewed[Journal of Empirical Legal Studies article](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jels.12413) , Varun Magesh and five coauthors reported that the versions of Lexis+ AI, Westlaw AI-Assisted Research, and Ask Practical Law AI they tested hallucinated between 17% and 33% of the time. The Lexis+ AI and Ask Practical Law AI queries ran from March 22 to April 22, 2024, while the Westlaw AI-Assisted Research queries ran from May 23 to May 27, 2024. The findings therefore do not measure later product versions. The lasting lesson is narrower: a real link can point to material that does not support the proposition.


### Treat security as a use-specific decision


The controlling terms should state how prompts, files, outputs, logs, and feedback are used and retained. Access design should cover single sign-on (SSO), role-based access controls (RBAC), matter permissions, ethical walls, audit logs, deletion, subprocessors, and incident response. Our[confidential patent work guide](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/is-ai-safe-for-confidential-patent-work) explains how those controls apply to sensitive IP matters.


[ABA Formal Opinion 512](https://www.americanbar.org/content/dam/aba/administrative/professional_responsibility/ethics-opinions/aba-formal-opinion-512.pdf) connects lawyers’ use of generative AI to duties of competence, confidentiality, communication, supervision, candor, and reasonable fees. The lawyer remains responsible for the work and for selecting a level of review appropriate to the tool and task.


### Run a narrow pilot with known answers


A focused pilot should use representative documents, difficult edge cases, a human baseline, named reviewers, and a defined acceptance rule. Record setup, generation, source review, correction, export, and administration time. Compare cost per accepted output rather than cost per generated output. Our[patent AI pilot checklist](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/how-to-evaluate-ai-for-patent-work) provides a detailed model for specialist legal workflows.


### Count the full operating cost


Public seat prices reveal only part of the spend. Include content subscriptions, usage credits, implementation, integrations, security review, training, administration, attorney review, corrections, and exit costs. The right economic unit may be an accepted chart, reviewed contract, coded gigabyte, completed matter, or active seat, depending on the workflow.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is there a legal version of ChatGPT?


Yes. CoCounsel Legal, Lexis+ with Protégé, Harvey, and Paxton all provide conversational legal assistants connected to legal sources or controlled organizational material. Practice-specific tools add narrower workflows and evidence. These systems can support legal work, while the attorney retains responsibility for the analysis, advice, and filings.


### Can lawyers use free AI tools?


Free consumer AI can help with low-risk brainstorming or generic text that contains no client information. It is a poor default for confidential matter data, legal authority, or final work product. A firm-approved environment with written data terms, appropriate access controls, source grounding, and attorney review is the safer baseline.


### Which legal AI tool fits a small law firm?


The answer follows the bottleneck. Clio addresses practice operations and matter-connected legal work. Paxton combines U.S. research, drafting, and file analysis in a self-serve plan. Spellbook focuses on contracts in Word and Google Docs, with multi-document work in Associate. For patent litigation, our platform provides a self-serve path from prior art and product evidence to source-linked claim charts.


### Will legal AI replace lawyers?


Current legal AI tools can retrieve, classify, summarize, draft, and automate defined steps. Lawyers remain responsible for advice, strategy, and final work product. These capabilities do not establish how legal employment will change.
